subject: Cashflow smoothing: credit collar proposal and VAT allocation
messages:
From: Anna Walsh <anna@clearwave.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearWave Finance <finance@clearwave.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Contract draft & billing — Net60 request

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the updated SOW. We reviewed with Finance and procurement is asking if Redwood can accommodate Net60 instead of Net30 for the first 3 invoices of the engagement given our Q3 cashflow plan.

A few specifics from their side:
- Target payment cadence: Net60 for first three monthly invoices, then Net30 moving forward.
- They want a small credit collar (10% of monthly invoice) to be retained until month 4 as a contingency for usage variance.
- VAT: ClearWave will be responsible for VAT in the EU, but we need Redwood to confirm how VAT will appear on the invoice and whether you can split amounts so our local VAT reclaim team can process faster.

Is this something Redwood can support? If needed, we can loop in procurement for a short call.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Walsh
Head of Procurement, ClearWave Analytics

Attachment: CW-billing-ask-0904.pdf (summary of request)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Anna Walsh <anna@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract draft & billing — Net60 request

Anna — thanks for the clear note and the PDF. I'm copying Marcus (Finance) and Marissa (Sales Ops) to confirm the operational side.

High-level thoughts:
1) Net60 for the first three invoices is something we can consider, but we would like to balance it with either: a) a small deposit up front equal to one month's committed minimum, or b) the credit collar being 10% as you proposed and formally held as a retention on the invoices.
2) VAT presentation: we can break out VAT line items on each invoice and include the VAT registration details for Redwood in the EU. That should speed your reclaim process.
3) To avoid long tail exposure for Redwood, propose a staged catch-up clause: if any of the first three invoices are unpaid past Net60+14 days, Redwood can convert upcoming invoices to Net30 and trigger the deposit/retention.

I'll attach an updated payment-plan spreadsheet with two alternatives: "Deposit + Net60" and "No deposit + 10% collar, staged catch-up." Marcus — can you confirm whether Finance is comfortable with the staged catch-up and the legal team's preferences on how the collar is described on the invoice?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW-CW-v2.pdf, redline-payment-plan.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract draft & billing — Net60 request

Mina/Marissa — quick run from Finance:
- Net60 for the first three invoices is acceptable provided we have either: a) a refundable deposit (one month's committed MRR) collected before the SOW start, or b) a formal retention (10%) line on invoices with funds held until month 4.
- Preference: deposit, because it reduces receivables risk and simplifies accounting treatment; retention requires a separate liability line on our books for the held funds and slightly more bookkeeping overhead.
- VAT: we'll issue the invoice with VAT broken out. For EU customers with local VAT reclaim, we can include our VAT ID and a short note stating "Customer liable for VAT" where applicable. Need final confirmation on ClearWave VAT entity id to put on invoice.

If ClearWave is firm on not providing a deposit upfront, Finance will accept the 10% retention but requests the staged catch-up clause Mina proposed be drafted into the payment terms.

Marcus
VP Finance, Redwood Inference

If we can get the updated SOW + payment schedule with those two items formalized, we can sign and route for internal approvals.

Best,
Anna

Anna — great, thanks for the confirmation and for sending the VAT ID. We've updated the SOW and payment-plan:
- No upfront deposit; retention=10% on invoices 1–3 labeled exactly as you requested. The retained amounts will appear as a liability in Redwood's ledger and then be released as a credit on invoice 4 (applied automatically).
- Payment terms: invoices 1–3 Net60, then Net30 thereafter. If any invoice becomes >Net74 (Net60+14) without remediation, Redwood may convert future invoices to Net30 until outstanding balances are cleared.
- Invoice format: top-level subtotal, VAT line, retention line, and then final amount due. We'll add your VAT ID to the invoice template.

Attached: updated SOW (SOW-CW-v2.pdf) and the payment-plan spreadsheet (redline-payment-plan.xlsx). Also linking the HubSpot deal and a DocuSign envelope (see links).

Next step: I'll prepare a short addendum to the SOW reflecting the retention and staged catch-up clause and upload to DocuSign. Can you confirm signatory name and email for ClearWave?

Thanks,
Mina
